pending_qa.q: What makes the current El Niño a 'Super El Niño' and how strong is it?
pending_qa.r: Federal forecasters describe it as a very strong El Niño, with climate scientist Julia Cole noting it is stronger than any other El Niño has been at this time of year. Temperatures are still rising, and researchers expect this developing El Niño to be historic and probably record-breaking, with impacts potentially lasting for months after it peaks at year-end.

pending_qa.q: What are the projected temperature impacts of this Super El Niño in the United States?
pending_qa.r: This El Niño will raise temperatures globally, and since it occurs on top of climate change when the planet is already about 2.5 degrees Fahrenheit hotter from fossil fuels, this year or next year could become the hottest year on record.

pending_qa.q: How does rainfall distribution differ across the US during El Niño years?
pending_qa.r: During El Niño years, the southern half of the US usually experiences more intense rain that could cause destructive flooding, while the northern half gets drier, which is significant for the Intermountain West already facing drought and low snowfall.

pending_qa.q: Are modern El Niños stronger than historical ones, and what causes this difference?
pending_qa.r: Climate scientist Julia Cole studied coral skeletons in the Galapagos covering the past thousand years and found that modern El Niños are significantly stronger than those in the pre-industrial era. Today's El Niños are about 36 percent stronger, suggesting that strong El Niño events are a consequence of being in a warmer world.

pending_qa.q: What is the current measles situation in Pennsylvania and what deaths have been reported?
pending_qa.r: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced two deaths linked to measles, described as the first measles deaths in 2026 and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years. However, Governor Shapiro released extremely limited information about the deceased, citing privacy concerns, which fueled online theories that they may not have occurred or were not caused by measles.

pending_qa.q: What was Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s response to the Pennsylvania measles deaths?
pending_qa.r: Secretary Kennedy questioned whether the deaths were real, saying 'We're trying to figure out who those deaths were and whether they actually happened, and we can't figure that out yet.' He also suggested the measles vaccine contains fetal tissue, which is false, did not offer condolences to the families, and did not urge unvaccinated people in affected areas to get the MMR vaccine.

pending_qa.q: What false claims has Kennedy made about vaccines during his tenure as Health Secretary?
pending_qa.r: Kennedy suggested the measles vaccine has fetal tissue in it, which it does not. Additionally, Democratic members of Congress charged that he lied to Congress during his confirmation hearing about a 2019 trip to Samoa during a measles outbreak, claiming it had nothing to do with vaccines when new documents suggest it very much did.

pending_qa.q: How long has the US military operation in Iran been ongoing and what were the stated objectives?
pending_qa.r: President Trump launched what he called major combat operations in Iran six months ago, stating the goal was to eliminate immediate threats posed by the regime and support the Iranian people. When pressed for a timeline, Trump said the operation would take four or five weeks, but six months later it is clear to many observers that none of those stated objectives have been met.

pending_qa.q: What is the current economic situation for Iranian citizens and how severe is inflation?
pending_qa.r: Life in Iran is very difficult and challenging for both people and government. Inflation is projected to be almost 70 percent, with the Iranian currency dropping to its lowest level this week, trading at more than two million rials to the dollar, and there is little evidence that economic pressure has been effective in changing Iranian policy.

pending_qa.q: Has Iran experienced any military success or losses during the six months of conflict?
pending_qa.r: Iran survived an unprecedented attack, but it has come at a cost with very difficult conditions on many fronts for the people. Six months of war and more than four months of a naval blockade aimed at choking off the Iranian economy have created widespread hardship.

pending_qa.q: What is public opinion in Iran regarding the US and Israeli attacks?
pending_qa.r: Early on there were some Iranian voices in support of US and Israeli attacks hoping for regime change, but those voices have been muted in recent months. While many people are having a hard time economically and want the pressure to ease, what has been seen publicly over the past several months is an almost daily presence of many people who view this as a war for survival and are supporting the government.
